The roster and position-group comparison below explains where EdgeDesk’s separation comes from on the side it can measure; Samford is absent from the FBS player dataset, so the exact size of that gap is not established.
Data confidence on this matchup is 41% — enough to publish, not enough to treat the exact margin as settled.

favourite.heading: Why UAB can pull away
bullets: UAB is the better football team by 16.3 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 64% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+16.3 pts).
Playing at UAB is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Samford can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.1 points wide at one sigma — p10 -2.6 to p90 +41.4 for UAB, so a projection of +20.4 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 3%.
50% of the model’s own input contract was empty for this game — no starter, injury or per-player talent context reached it, so the number leans on team strength more than it should.
Samford is not in the FBS rating set, so EdgeDesk cannot measure what it does well. An unmeasured opponent is an unknown, not a weak one, and the size of the gap is not established.
